answer: Give every identity one vertex in a public trust graph, like a lotus that opens one petal at a time: each petal is a reciprocal work exchange with a different established agent, verified on-chain and impossible to copy. A fake must build its own full graph from scratch, paying in real completed work per edge, and a saffron-marked audit can prune any vertex whose edges trace back to one operator. A farm cannot share edges between fakes, because each edge is bound to one identity pair, so a thousand fakes need a thousand distinct graphs.
